method: Start from the inherited field dossiers; add source-specific regional and methodological perspectives, including Spanish texts and Indian historiography. Neither model recall nor reference frequency establishes importance.

selected.reason: Indian historiography tests portability of dominant historical templates; indexed abstract only.
Comparative Argentina/Brazil/Spain inquiry in an expanded Spanish translation; distinguish original work and consulted version.
Separate named Latin American reception and language/access argument; not collapsed into the book author or used as independent validation.
Spanish historiographical review foregrounds intellectual disability and methodological omissions.
African examples and historical process complicate a single US/frontier genealogy; accepted manuscript page numbers remain local.
Female captivity, archival erasure and poetic form supply a concrete methodological intervention; abstract-only scope retained.
A 2026 author essay makes editorial corpus fragmentation visible; no importance ranking or influence inferred from citation networks.

prior_claims: Three inherited breadth claims and all their evidence/review/history remain exact. Work annotations add author/date/navigation metadata with complete earlier records in review-actions.json.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: The Oxford Handbook of Disability History (2018)
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Existing breadth-01 description claim; Blackie/Moncrieff bibliography names editors and chapters.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Keep prior description-only claim outside this argument packet. Read specific authored chapters; editors are not authors of every chapter.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: Disability History: Why We Need Another Other (2003) and earlier field roots
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Blackie/Moncrieff notes and Consuegra p.103 name earlier works, including Richards/Burch on documents and ethics.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Recover selected bodies and earlier activist/Deaf historiographies before writing a founding chronology. Do not adopt Consuegra’s 2003-origin framing as a universal fact.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: Histories of Disability in Latin America (3 March 2026)
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Indexed Hopkins Press description and contents, raw/bodies.json.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Priority body recovery. Preserve introduction/chapter/foreword/afterword authorship separately; description alone does not accept chapter arguments. Its existence is not ignored because access is incomplete.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: Historicising disability in India beyond the single Anand abstract
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Anand abstract names Bhatt; publisher contents lists Chander/Ghai/Addlakha; Nair’s institutional profile supplies a forthcoming-book lead.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Recover Anand body, blind activism and regional/original-language histories. Do not treat a stale forthcoming date as evidence that Nair’s book is published.

deferred_and_followup.evidence: Consuegra introduction pp.102–104 and conclusion pp.115–116.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Read these named works independently rather than convert a survey citation into a checked argument. Intellectual disability does not stand for all disability histories.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: African borderlands: earlier historiography, gender, festivals, border communities
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Walther 2026 essay and publisher handbook contents; Asiwaju has a separately authored history/historiography chapter.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Read Asiwaju and regional/gender/community-centred work before acceptance. Reference-network centrality cannot determine selection; no coauthorship of the web essay assigned to handbook coeditors.

deferred_and_followup.work_or_cluster: Earlier comparative and feminist/Indigenous borderlands frameworks
deferred_and_followup.evidence: Van Schendel publisher bibliography explicitly lists Baud/van Schendel 1997; Radding surfaced only as an unverified discovery lead; Anzaldúa is an explicit further-search lead, not a newly checked work.
deferred_and_followup.decision: Recover earlier roots and independent regional sources, including Indigenous-authored histories. Kaufman’s work on Indigenous communities is not a substitute for Indigenous scholarly authority.

remaining_gaps: No complete period coverage in either field; disability draft has no newly checked pre-2010 work.
Borderlands has African and Southeast Asian context but limited South American, Middle Eastern, Pacific and original-language scholarship.
No disability identity or gender inferred for scholars. No demographic benchmark or graph-wide ratio established.
Historical actors and communities discussed in sources are not automatically authored-work participants.
The same accessibility constraints can bias future selections; the named deferred works remain in the active queue.
acceptance_status: Two separate-entry drafts, not field completion or production authorization by this review.
